landmarks.name: Mount Kenya
landmarks.writeup: The highest mountain in Kenya and the second-highest in Africa, known for its unique alpine ecosystem.

wiki.extract: Mount Kenya is the second highest mountain in Africa. Located about 150 km north-northeast of the capital Nairobi and just 16.5 kilometres south of the equator, the mountain's highest peaks are Batian, Nelion, and Point Lenana. Historically situated in the former Eastern and Central provinces, the massif now serves as the intersection of Meru, Embu, Kirinyaga, Nyeri, and Tharaka Nithi counties. The area was officially gazetted as the Mount Kenya National Park in 1949 and was later designated a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1997 for its outstanding natural beauty and ecological significance. Today, the park and its surrounding forest reserve are managed by the Kenya Wildlife Service and the Kenya Forest Service as a critical sanctuary for endangered species and a primary water tower for the region.

landmarks.name: Maasai Mara National Reserve
landmarks.writeup: A renowned wildlife reserve famous for the Great Migration and diverse wildlife including lions, elephants, and cheetahs.

wiki.extract: Maasai Mara, sometimes also spelt Masai Mara and locally known simply as The Mara, is a large national game reserve in Narok County, Kenya, contiguous with the Serengeti National Park in Tanzania. It is named in honour of the Maasai people, the ancestral inhabitants of the area, who migrated to the area from the Nile Basin. Their description of the area when looked at from afar: "Mara" means "spotted" in the Maa language because of the short bushy trees which dot the landscape.

landmarks.name: Lake Nakuru
landmarks.writeup: A soda lake known for its large populations of flamingos and diverse bird species.

wiki.extract: Nakuru, sometimes referred to as Nakuru City, is the capital city of Nakuru County, Kenya. As of 2019, Nakuru had an urban population of 570,674. The city lies along the Nairobi–Nakuru Highway, 160 kilometres (99 mi) from Nairobi, the capital city of Kenya. In December 2021, Nakuru City became the fourth urban area in Kenya to be assigned the status of "city".

landmarks.name: Lamu Old Town
landmarks.writeup: A UNESCO World Heritage site, this historic Swahili settlement features traditional architecture and rich cultural heritage.

wiki.extract: Lamu or Lamu Town is a small town on Lamu Island, which in turn is a part of the Lamu Archipelago in Kenya on the continent of Africa. Situated 341 kilometres (212 mi) by road northeast of Mombasa that ends at Mokowe Jetty, from where the sea channel has to be crossed to reach Lamu Island, it is the headquarter of Lamu County and a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

landmarks.name: Nairobi National Park
landmarks.writeup: A unique wildlife park located just outside Nairobi, home to lions, rhinos, and giraffes.

wiki.extract:
Nairobi National Park is a national park in Kenya that was established in 1946 about 7 km (4.3 mi) south of Nairobi. It is fenced on three sides, whereas the open southern boundary allows migrating wildlife to move between the park and the adjacent Kitengela plains. Herbivores gather in the park during the dry season. Nairobi National Park is negatively affected by increasing human and livestock populations, changing land use and poaching of wildlife.
Despite its proximity to the city and its relative small size, it boasts a large and varied wildlife population, and is one of Kenya's most successful rhinoceros sanctuaries.

cultural_events.name: Maasai Mara Wildebeest Migration
cultural_events.writeup: An annual natural event where millions of wildebeest migrate across the Mara River, attracting tourists worldwide.

cultural_events.name: Lamu Cultural Festival
cultural_events.writeup: A celebration of Swahili culture featuring traditional music, dance, dhow races, and crafts.

cultural_events.name: Mombasa Carnival
cultural_events.writeup: A vibrant festival showcasing coastal culture, music, and dance.

food_writeup: Kenyan cuisine features staples like ugali (maize porridge), sukuma wiki (collard greens), nyama choma (grilled meat), and a variety of stews and fresh vegetables reflecting diverse ethnic influences.
brief_history: Kenya gained independence from British colonial rule in 1963. It has a rich history shaped by indigenous communities, Arab traders, and European colonization. Post-independence, Kenya has developed into a key economic and political hub in East Africa.

important_people.name: Jomo Kenyatta
important_people.description: First President of Kenya and a founding father of the nation.

important_people.name: Wangari Maathai
important_people.description: Environmentalist and Nobel Peace Prize laureate.

important_people.name: Eliud Kipchoge
important_people.description: World-renowned long-distance runner and Olympic champion.

current_conflicts: Kenya faces challenges including political tensions, occasional ethnic clashes, and security threats from extremist groups such as Al-Shabaab.
